twitter.content: On Durability of the tariff regime after the SCOTUS IEEPA ruling — our position: Tariffs are leverage paid by foreigners; AI supremacy is a national-security imperative; deals over rules
On AI capex supercycle versus bubble / bond-market financing strain — our position: Commitment to win-win trade and opposition to weaponizing supply chains while pursuing self-reliance
On US-China chip export controls and the 25% revenue-share model — our position: Supports American AI leadership but lobbies to keep every market including China open; controls should be narrow
On Rare-earth/magnet chokepoint and the Nov 27 2026 truce expiry — our position: Customer neutrality and commitment to Taiwan as tech heart, while hedging via a US footprint
On Semiconductor reshoring and Taiwan concentration risk — our position: AI demand is insatiable and spending is disciplined; owning the full stack is strategic
On Wide-but-shallow AI adoption and small near-term productivity gains — our position: Safe AGI for humanity while racing to lock up compute and sovereign geographic deals
On Sovereign AI and state equity in strategic chip firms — our position: Data-dependent and apolitical; treats tariff price effects as arguably transitory
On Data-center energy demand as the binding compute input — our position: Constitutional limits and separation of powers; SCOTUS ruled IEEPA does not authorize tariffs
On Connector economies and statistical vs. real decoupling — our position: Open research and self-reliance; algorithmic efficiency beats brute-force compute hoarding
On Durability of the tariff regime after the SCOTUS IEEPA ruling — our position: Strategic autonomy and open trade, negotiating to avoid US tariffs while under-building compute
